discovery: Prediction and precision measurement of the acoustic oscillations in the cosmic microwave background anisotropies, establishing the standard cosmological model

nominees.name: Rashid Sunyaev
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics, Garching; Space Research Institute (IKI), Moscow

motivation: Sunyaev (with the late Zeldovich) predicted that sound waves in the primordial photon-baryon plasma leave a characteristic acoustic imprint on the cosmic microwave background. Bennett led WMAP, which mapped the full-sky temperature and polarization anisotropies with the precision needed to resolve these acoustic peaks. Puget, as Principal Investigator of Planck's High Frequency Instrument, brought the measurements to the cosmic-variance limit across the primary temperature spectrum. Together, these theoretical and experimental achievements turned cosmology into a precision science. They fixed the geometry, age, and matter and baryon content of the Universe to percent-level accuracy. They showed that the primordial fluctuations are adiabatic, Gaussian and nearly scale-invariant, with a measured departure from exact scale invariance, as inflation predicts. They also constrained the number and masses of neutrinos. The 2006 prize recognised the blackbody spectrum and the discovery of anisotropy. This nomination recognises the acoustic physics and the precision measurements that established the standard model of cosmology.
